speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs in light of the two reports presented by the UN Fact-Finding Mission in September 2018, how can ASEAN further help to resolve the crisis related to the Rakhine State, which has caused a catastrophic human tragedy in and around Myanmar.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs in light of the two reports presented by the UN Fact-Finding Mission in September 2018, whether Myanmar can be compelled to abide by Articles 14, 15, 22, 28, 31(2), read with Article 2, of the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration as well as Article 2, paragraph 2(i), Article 20, paragraph 4 and Article 7, paragraph (2)(e) of the ASEAN Charter.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs whether Singapore will (i) send another consignment of humanitarian supplies to Bangladesh to provide aid for Rohingya refugees this year and (ii) consider increasing Singapore's financial contribution to the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) next year.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The United Nations (UN) Human Rights Council (UNHRC) appointed a fact-finding mission in March last year.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This fact-finding mission on Myanmar published its full Report on 18 September.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: This Report contained harrowing accounts of brutal and shocking atrocities committed in the Rakhine State that led to an outflow of refugees to Bangladesh.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On 29 September, we had an Informal Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Foreign Ministers' meeting.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, because this topic was so sensitive, we convened a smaller group consisting of only the Ministers.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We expressed our grave concern with these alleged acts of violence that had led to loss of lives, injuries, destructions of homes and displacement of large numbers of people.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And to be brutally honest, this is a man-made humanitarian disaster and something which should not be happening in this day and age.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we emphasised that a key milestone now must surely be the start or the commencement of a repatriation of refugees to Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we are going to have to wait and see and hope that this will begin shortly.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We also urged the government of Myanmar to step up its implementation of all the recommendations of the Kofi Annan Advisory Commission on Rakhine State, because the root causes of this conflict need to be addressed.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And a conducive environment needs to be created so that all affected communities can rebuild their lives.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: You need circumstances in which there are opportunities for reconciliation for assurances of justice and equality and, ultimately, for better prospects for all communities.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Otherwise, this long-term intercommunal complex situation will fester.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And if this festers, it will create more opportunities for extremism and, ultimately, terrorism, which will not respect boundaries, and will represent a clear and present threat throughout Southeast Asia and beyond.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In the meantime, the refugees in Bangladesh deserve and need assistance.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Members will recall that, in fact, last year, we had sent a consignment of assistance to the refugees in Bangladesh.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Depending on assessment of their future needs, we may have to do so again.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And they do need to do the right thing and to do the right thing for all the vulnerable, defenceless and innocent victims.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is also a salutary warning to all of us in Southeast Asia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Race, language and religion are live issues and can always be exploited for short-term political gains.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But an unfair share of the burden and of the injuries are sustained by defenceless people.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Following the UN Fact-Finding Mission report in September of this year, the UNHRC took the additional step of deciding to set up a team to investigate further alleged atrocities.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Singapore is not currently a Council member on UNHRC.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, these decisions, we are not party to.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: For instance, the Fact-Finding Mission did not have any cooperation from Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, all the accounts which are contained in the report are based on interviews conducted with refugees outside Myanmar.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In this Independent Commission are two foreigners – one, a Filipino ambassador and another one from Japan.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Both of them have reputations for being fiercely independent.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As of now, we are waiting for the Independent Commission to begin its work, submit its report, and we will listen with great interest, particularly to the two independent members of the Commission.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think we have to be practical and we have to look for every opportunity in which not to inflame the situation, but nevertheless, can hold people who are responsible fully accountable.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In his reply, I think he said that he was doing assessment on the ground to see whether to send a second consignment to Bangladesh.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I just check when this assessment will be completed?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that the United States (US) had done an assessment and, just last week, they announced that they will double the aid to refugees in Bangladesh and Myanmar.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have been on the ground in the refugee camps in Bangladesh.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have seen what conditions they are living in.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have heard the stories firsthand of how much they have suffered, seen children with bullet wounds and how they have been scarred for life.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And the people there really do need help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that there had been many landslides recently as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: So, I am really hopeful that Singapore will provide this second consignment of humanitarian aid.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There is a second part of my Parliamentary Question (PQ), and it is whether we will increase our financial contributions to UNHRC so that we can help refugees around the world rebuild their lives.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The answer to the first question is that we are in touch with the Bangladesh government.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But my concern goes beyond just humanitarian assistance.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And a long-term solution is a political solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In addition to that, you also want to have deterrence from future bouts of violence.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why having Independent Commissions of Inquiry and holding people accountable are important.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Member's second question on our support for UNHCR, we are one of the countries that make voluntary contributions.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I do not want to over inflate the importance of that.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: We will do our part and we will work with UNHCR.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While I understand that we need time to let the independent Commission of Inquiry to take place but, beyond that, Singapore is the ASEAN Chair.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I think there was a related question that Member Christopher de Souza also had asked.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And the short answer to that, as far as ASEAN is concerned, is no.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But what we can do is through moral suasion, persuasion, transparency and keeping this on the agenda.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And also telling the Myanmar government that we want and hope for a long-term viable, good outcome, and that ASEAN stands ready to help.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But Members also need to understand that ASEAN is an association that makes decisions by consensus.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Once you understand that every decision requires consensus, it effectively means every single country has a veto.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, that acts as a constraint to the legal options available.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I have said, in any case, ultimately, the long-term solution for this is a political solution.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And politics must involve discussion, disagreement, dispute resolution if need be, and hoping that, in the long run, cool heads will prevail and people will do the right thing.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Compulsion, tempting as it is, usually almost never works in these sorts of situations.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I do understand that a long-term political solution is needed.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: But while the rest of the world debates and gives advice and coaxed and persuades through moral suasion, is there something that Singaporeans can do more?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know that it is a controversial topic if we want to use taxpayers' money to do more, but can the Government – the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) or the Ministry of Education (MOE) – organise local efforts so that we can raise funds and people can contribute for a cause that is bigger than themselves?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I thought this would be a great chance for us to look beyond Singapore, what we are blessed with, and look at how we can contribute to what are called disasters in the world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: There is probably a lot more that we are not even aware of.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Whilst in the totality of it, we are probably a drop in the ocean.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I just wanted to commend that the attitude that the Member has always espoused, in fact, is being practised.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would expect that more assistance will flow.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And we will work together with the people sector on this.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: As I have said, this sort of situation should not be happening in this day and age.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is a stark reminder that we do not live in a perfect world.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: That is why I do not take an unnecessarily provocative and combative approach to this issue.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Second, have sufficient levels of transparency and accountability.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: It is not something that will be resolved even in 200 days.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, you do need a sense of realism, without giving up on hope and without giving up that sense of solidarity with fellow human beings.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, we will continue to do our best.
